items.stem: Why do historians resist describing the medieval period as simply a 'dark age'?

options.text: It saw significant intellectual, economic and institutional development, and the label reflects later polemic
options.rationale: Correct: the term distorts a varied, productive era and originates in Renaissance and later rhetoric.
Conflict was common; the point is the dismissive label.
Extensive records survive; the issue is the stereotype.

options.text: Because it lasted only fifty years
options.rationale: It spanned roughly a thousand years.

items.explanation: Correct: the term distorts a varied, productive era and originates in Renaissance and later rhetoric.

items.stem: Which TWO factors most directly help explain the rapid spread of the Reformation? (Select TWO.)

options.text: The printing press, which circulated ideas and texts widely
options.rationale: Correct: print multiplied and spread reform writings quickly.

options.text: The political interests of rulers who backed reform
options.rationale: Correct: princely support shaped where and how reform succeeded.

options.text: The invention of the steam engine
The founding of the United Nations

items.explanation: Correct: print multiplied and spread reform writings quickly.

items.stem: A textbook claims the First World War was 'inevitable because of one assassination'. What is the flaw?

options.text: A single trigger cannot explain the war without alliances, militarism, rivalries and decisions by many actors
options.rationale: Correct: the assassination was a trigger within a web of longer-term causes and choices.
It did happen; the flaw is reducing cause to it alone.

options.text: Wars are never caused by events
options.rationale: Events matter, but as part of wider causation.
No single factor suffices, including economics.

items.explanation: Correct: the assassination was a trigger within a web of longer-term causes and choices.
